subject: Clarify queueing & throughput guarantees — proposed SLA addendum
messages:
From: Sophia Liu <sophia@clearwater-med.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearwater-med.com
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity guarantees — queueing behavior clarification and addendum request

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we work the internal signoff for the Dedicated capacity order, the legal and SRE teams at Clearwater asked for clearer language about two operational behaviors before we finalize the PO:

1) During scheduled maintenance and region failover, what level of reserved throughput will be preserved for our reserved GPU pool? We need a concrete minimum (tokens/sec or p95 throughput) for the duration of any rolling maintenance.
2) Queueing / priority behavior: if other customers are bursting, can our reserved capacity be preempted? If so, please describe the preemption windows and expected tail-latency degradation.

We started a draft SLO document to show what we need — attached. Can Redwood provide a redline or a short addendum to the master services agreement that spells out the minimum sustained throughput and queue priority rules (including any crediting or mitigations)?

Attaching: Clearwater_SLO_Specs.xlsx

Sophia Liu
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
Clearwater Medical
[Attachment: Clearwater_SLO_Specs.xlsx]
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Liu <sophia@clearwater-med.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guarantees — queueing behavior clarification and addendum request

Hi Sophia — thanks, and appreciate the clarity in the spreadsheet. High level: we can cover both asks with an SLA addendum tied to your reserved pool. Two quick notes up front:

- Minimum preserved throughput: we can commit to a sustained throughput floor measured as tokens/sec per reserved-GPU-equivalent over maintenance windows (we'll propose a numeric floor in the redline).
- Preemption / queue priority: Reserved pools are first-class and have isolation by default; however, under extreme capacity pressure (region-wide failover or unprecedented burst) we may preempt soft-burst capacity. We do not preempt reserved capacity without notice unless ordered by a cross-region control-plane failover.

I'm looping in Lauren for technical wording (how to measure and report the throughput floor) and Ben for procurement/pricing impact. We have a preliminary draft attached. If it looks good we can push a redline and send to your legal team.

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood to send redline SLA addendum (target: 48 business hours)
- Clearwater to confirm the preferred measurement metric (tokens/sec vs. p95 request throughput)
- Legal and procurement exchange DocuSign once redline is agreed

[Attachment: proposed-sla-draft.docx]

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-sla-draft.docx]
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-19T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guarantees — queueing behavior clarification and addendum request

David / team — technical input below that we should fold into the addendum. I recommend explicit language and a measurement example so there's no ambiguity during incidents.

Suggested clauses (high level):
- Measurement unit: "sustained tokens/sec per reserved GPU-equivalent measured as a 5-minute rolling average at the model endpoint ingress". This avoids per-request p95 variability.
- Maintenance windows: during scheduled maintenance (notice window >= 72 hours) we will preserve at least 70% of baseline sustained throughput for the reserved pool for the first maintenance day; for multi-day migrations we provide an agreed ramp plan and credits for any deviation.
- Preemption behavior: reserved pools are isolated from best-effort burst queues; hard preemption of reserved GPUs will only occur for catastrophic cross-region failover and requires coordination with the account team. In those events, tail-latency mitigation: Redwood will route to a compatible model variant in another region or provide token-based credits for impacted windows.

Operational notes for the addendum:
- Reporting: we'll push per-minute throughput graphs into your console and deliver a post-incident throughput report.
- Credits: propose a sliding credit scale tied to % of preserved throughput vs. committed. I'll attach numbers separately.

Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/dedicated-queueing

Lauren
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guarantees — pricing implications

Couple quick pricing notes for the redline:

- Adding a guaranteed maintenance-preserved floor (e.g., 70% sustained throughput) increases provider-side headroom requirements; recommend a 12% uplift on the reserved monthly commitment to cover capacity redundancy. I'll attach an impact workbook with scenarios.
- Credits formula: suggest credit = (Committed throughput - preserved throughput) / Committed throughput * monthly reserved fee * credit-weighting. We can soften the weighting for scheduled maintenance.

I'll include worked examples in pricing-impact.xlsx. If Clearwater pushes back, we can offer a one-time onboarding credit instead of a permanent uplift for the first 3 months.

Ben Carter
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing-impact.xlsx]
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Liu <sophia@clearwater-med.com>, procurement@clearwater-med.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T10:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guarantees — proposed SLA addendum and next steps

Sophia — thanks for the patience. Attached is a redlined SLA addendum that incorporates Lauren's measurement language and Ben's pricing options. Key highlights in plain language:

- Sustained throughput floor: committed as X tokens/sec per reserved-GPU-equivalent (redline contains the exact numeric floor and sample calculations).
- Maintenance handling: scheduled maintenance preserved throughput minimum: 70% of baseline for the first 24 hours; multi-day migrations require a ramp plan.
- Preemption: reserved pools are isolated; hard preemption only on catastrophic cross-region events with coordination.
- Credits: sliding-scale credit with a softened factor for scheduled maintenance; onboarding credit option for the first 3 months is included as an alternative.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm preferred measurement (tokens/sec vs. p95) — default in the redline is tokens/sec.
2) If that matches, I'll send the DocuSign redline to your legal team and route to our finance for PO alignment (Deal: DEAL-2026-1174).
3) Ben will send a short commercial note with the uplift vs. no-uplift options for procurement.

Redlines and pricing impact attached. DocuSign link below for preliminary legal review: https://www.docusign.com/en/redline/ABC-REDLINE-789

Regards,
David Kim
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redline-sla-addendum.pdf]
